title: FoundMyFitness Topic - Protein Intake
abstract:
## Lifespan and Longevity: The Role of IGF and mTOR  
### Does high protein accelerate aging?  
Some researchers argue that **a high protein intake, particularly from animal sources, may increase cancer risk and accelerate aging**. This hypothesis is based on laboratory studies in animals and observational studies in humans. For instance, one study found that middle-aged adults consuming high-protein diets (20% of daily calories) [were 75% more likely to die from any cause and four times more likely to die from cancer.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24606898/) However, these risks often disappear when [accounting for other lifestyle factors such as obesity, smoking, heavy drinking, or sedentary behavior](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamainternalmedicine/fullarticle/2540540). Among healthy individuals, **high-protein diets do not show the same associations with mortality, suggesting that lifestyle context is crucial**.
### IGF-1 is a double-edged sword  
Protein-rich diets, especially those high in animal protein, increase IGF-1 levels. **IGF-1 supports muscle growth, repair, and brain health but may also promote the survival of precancerous cells**, potentially raising cancer risk. However, overly low IGF-1 levels have their own risks, such as impaired brain health, as evidenced by studies showing brain matter loss with extreme calorie restriction.  
Recent research highlights a [U-shaped relationship between IGF-1 levels and mortality](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35048526/), with both **very high and very low levels linked to increased death rates**. For most people, an optimal range of IGF-1 (120–160 ng/mL) may balance these risks, though these recommendations are often aimed at sedentary individuals, not active ones.
### Athletes live longer despite high-protein diets  
If protein and IGF-1 were inherently harmful, athletes—who consume higher protein diets and have elevated IGF-1 levels—should experience shorter lifespans. Yet, the opposite is true. [Athletes consistently live 2–8 years longer than the general population](https://sportsmedicine-open.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s40798-015-0024-x) and have lower rates of cancer and cardiovascular disease. Regular physical activity ensures that **dietary protein and IGF-1 are used for repair and growth, not pathways associated with disease**.
